art-1: The seven constituent peoples and all the communities who share their land, united in the confederated States and the confederal autonomous municipalities listed in Article 1 bis, form the Balkan Confederation (Balkanska Konfederacija).
art-2: The Balkan Confederation protects the liberty and the rights of its peoples and of every person, and safeguards the independence and the security of the country.
art-3: The confederated States are sovereign except to the extent that their sovereignty is limited by the Confederal Constitution; they exercise all rights that are not vested in the Confederation.
art-4: The national language of the Confederation is the južnoslovenski jezik. It is expressed through three regional standards, western, central and eastern, equal in dignity and in law (Article 128).
art-5: Principles of public activity governed by the rule of law
The law is the basis and the limit of the activity of the Confederation, the States and the municipalities.
art-6: The allocation and the performance of public tasks are based on the principle of subsidiarity.
art-7: Every person is responsible for himself and contributes, according to his abilities, to the tasks of the community and of society.
art-7bis: The flag of the Confederation consists of a vertical red band at the hoist and a field of three horizontal bands, blue, white and blue. It is the flag of citizens and of municipal authorities.
art-1bis: The Balkan Confederation is composed of fifty-two States: forty-eight territorial States and four confederal territories. Two confederal autonomous municipalities, which are not States, are also attached to it.
art-1ter: The institutions of the Confederation are distributed among four capitals:
art-1quater: Definition and status of autonomous entities
Within certain States, autonomous entities are constituted in order to guarantee the cultural, educational and municipal rights of minority communities.
art-1quinquies: The autonomous entities recognised by the Constitution are:
art-1sexies: The territorial limits of an autonomous entity may not be altered without the consent of the majority of its inhabitants expressed by referendum.
art-1septies: The confederal autonomous municipalities of Brčko and Mostar are directly under confederal jurisdiction. They are attached to no State.
art-1octies: The Council of Communities (Veće Zajednica) represents before the confederal institutions the communities which belong to no constituent people and have autonomous entities: the Albanian, Hungarian, Slovak and Turkish communities.
art-8: Human dignity must be respected and protected.
art-9: All human beings are equal before the law.
art-10: Protection against arbitrary conduct and principle of good faith
Every person has the right to be treated by the authorities without arbitrariness and in good faith.
art-11: Right to life and to personal liberty
Every human being has the right to life. The death penalty is prohibited.
art-12: Protection of children and young people
Children and young people have the right to the special protection of their integrity and to the encouragement of their development.
art-13: Right to assistance when in need
Persons in need and unable to provide for themselves have the right to assistance and care, and to the financial means required for a decent standard of living.
art-14: Every person has the right to privacy in his private and family life and in his home, and in relation to his correspondence and communications by post and telecommunications.
art-15: Right to marry and to have a family
The right to marry and to have a family is guaranteed.
art-16: Freedom of conscience and belief is guaranteed.
art-17: Freedom of opinion and freedom of information are guaranteed.
art-18: Freedom of the press, radio and television and of other forms of dissemination of features and information by means of public telecommunications is guaranteed.
art-20: The right to an adequate basic education, free of charge, is guaranteed.
art-21: Freedom of teaching and of scientific research is guaranteed.
art-22: Freedom of artistic expression is guaranteed.
art-25: Citizens of the Confederation have the right to settle in any place within the confederal territory.
art-26: Protection against expulsion, extradition and deportation
Citizens of the Confederation may not be expelled; they may be extradited to a foreign authority only with their consent.
art-27: The right to own property is guaranteed.
art-29: Freedom of association of workers and employers
Workers, employers and their organisations have the right to join together in order to protect their interests, to form associations and to join or not to join such associations.
art-30: Every person whose case falls to be judged in judicial proceedings has the right to have his case heard by a legally constituted, competent, independent and impartial court. Ad hoc courts are prohibited.
art-31: No person may be deprived of his liberty other than in the circumstances and in the manner provided for by law.
art-32: Every person is presumed innocent until a final conviction has been pronounced.
art-33: Every person has the right to address petitions to the authorities without suffering any prejudice as a result.
art-35: Fundamental rights must be upheld throughout the legal system.
art-36: Restrictions on fundamental rights must have a legal basis. Significant restrictions must have their basis in a law. Cases of serious and immediate danger where no other course of action is possible are exempt.
art-37: Every person who declares his will to be a citizen and who is attached to a confederated State or to a confederal autonomous municipality is a citizen of the Confederation. Citizenship takes effect when the citizen card is issued.
art-38: Attachment is determined by the municipality of origin of the person, of one of his parents or of one of his grandparents; failing that, by his municipality of residence within the territory of the Confederation. It is not a matter of free choice.
art-39: The Confederation regulates the exercise of political rights at confederal level; the States regulate it at State and municipal level.
art-40: Citizens living abroad and the diaspora

The Confederation encourages relations among citizens living abroad and their relations with the Confederation. It may support organisations that pursue this objective, in particular in the occupied territories.
art-41: The Confederation and the States, as a complement to personal responsibility and private initiative, endeavour to ensure that:
art-42: The Confederation fulfils the tasks that are assigned to it by the Constitution.
art-43: Tasks of the States and allocation of tasks
The confederated States decide on the tasks that they are to fulfil within the scope of their powers.
art-44: The Confederation and the States support each other in the fulfilment of their tasks and cooperate with each other.
art-45: The States participate, in the cases provided for by the Constitution, in confederal decision-making, and in particular in the legislative process (Articles 106 bis and 122).
art-46: The States implement confederal law in accordance with the Constitution and the law.
art-47: The Confederation respects the autonomy of the States.
art-48: The States may enter into agreements with each other and establish common organisations and institutions. In particular, they may jointly undertake tasks of regional or local importance.
art-49: Declaration of general application and requirement to participate
At the request of interested States, the Confederation may declare inter-Balkan agreements to be generally binding or require States to participate in inter-Balkan agreements in the following areas:
art-50: Precedence of and compliance with confederal law
Confederal law takes precedence over any conflicting provision of the law of the States.
art-50bis: Where a State fails to comply with confederal law, the Konfederalno Veće gives it formal notice and sets a reasonable time limit for compliance. The State may apply to the Ustavni Sud.
art-51: The municipalities (opštine) are the basic communities of the Confederation. The municipality of origin establishes the attachment of citizens (Article 38).
art-52: Each State adopts a democratic constitution. This requires the approval of the people of the State and must be capable of being revised if the majority of those eligible to vote so request.
art-53: The Confederation protects the constitutional order of the States.
art-54: Existence, status and territory of the States
The Confederation protects the existence and status of the States, as well as their territory.
art-55: Foreign relations are the responsibility of the Confederation.
art-56: Participation of the States in foreign policy decisions
The confederated States are consulted on foreign policy decisions that affect their powers or their essential interests.
art-57: Relations between the States and foreign states
The confederated States may conclude treaties with foreign states on matters that lie within the scope of their powers.
art-58: The Confederation and the States ensure the security of the country and the protection of the population within the scope of their respective powers.
art-59: The Balkan Confederation has armed forces, the Konfederalne Oružane Snage. In principle, the armed forces are organised as a militia.
art-60: Every male citizen of the Confederation is required to do military service. The law provides for alternative civilian service, done on request, which lasts one and a half times as long as military service.
art-61: Organisation, training and equipment of the armed forces
Legislation on the armed forces and the organisation, training and equipment of the armed forces are the responsibility of the Confederation.
art-61bis: The armed forces are placed under the authority of the Konfederalno Veće, which exercises it through the Department of Defence and Security.
art-62: Legislation on civil defence is the responsibility of the Confederation; civil defence, under the direction of the Confederal Agency for Emergency Situations (KAVS; Konfederalna Agencija za Vanredne Situacije), has the task of protecting persons and property i…
art-63: Within the scope of their powers, the Confederation and the States jointly ensure a high level of quality in and accessibility to the Balkan Education Area (EBF).
art-64: School education is a matter for the confederated States.
art-65: The Confederation legislates on vocational education and training.
art-66: The Confederation runs the confederal polytechnic schools (KPU). It may establish, take over or run other higher education institutions and other institutions of higher education.
art-67: The Confederation promotes scientific research and innovation.
art-68: The Confederation lays down principles on continuing education and training.
art-69: The Confederation collects the statistical data required on the status and development of the population, the economy, society, education, research, the territory and the Balkan environment.
art-70: The Confederation may contribute to the confederated States' expenditure on education grants awarded to students at higher education and other institutions of higher education. It may promote the harmonisation of education grants between the States and lay dow…
art-71: In fulfilling their duties, the Confederation and the confederated States take account of the special need of children and young people for development and protection.
art-72: The Confederation and the confederated States support music education, in particular for children and young people.
art-73: The Confederation encourages sport, in particular training in sport at every level, recognising its importance for the health, well-being and social development of citizens.
art-73bis: In international football competitions, each constituent people is represented by its own national team. The law designates the other disciplines in which the same applies and governs the representation of the Confederation at multi-sport competitions.
art-74: Culture is a matter for the confederated States.
art-75: The national language of the Confederation is the južnoslovenski jezik, with its three regional standards: the western standard (Slovene speech), the central standard (Štokavian speech) and the eastern standard (Bulgarian and Macedonian speech) (Article 128).
art-76: The Confederation may promote Balkan film production and film culture.
art-77: The regulation of the relationship between religious communities and the State is the responsibility of the confederated States.
art-78: The Confederation and the confederated States endeavour to achieve a balanced and sustainable relationship between nature and its capacity to renew itself and the demands placed on it by the population.
art-79: The Confederation legislates on the protection of the population and its natural environment against damage or nuisance.
art-80: The Confederation lays down principles on spatial planning. Spatial planning is the responsibility of the confederated States and serves to ensure the appropriate and economic use of the land and its properly ordered settlement.
art-81: The national survey is the responsibility of the Confederation.
art-82: The proportion of second homes in the total stock of residential units and the residential gross floor area used in any municipality is restricted to a maximum of twenty per cent.
art-83: The Confederation, within the scope of its powers, ensures the economic use and the protection of water resources and provides protection against the harmful effects of water.
art-84: The Confederation ensures that the forests are able to fulfil their protective, commercial and public amenity functions.
art-85: Protection of nature, heritage and maritime areas
The protection of nature, of heritage, of maritime areas and of national parks is a matter for the confederated States.
art-86: The Confederation lays down principles on fishing and hunting, and in particular on preserving the diversity of fish species, wild mammals and birds.
art-87: The Confederation legislates on the protection of animals.
art-88: In the interest of the country or a large part of the country, the Confederation may build and operate public works or support their construction.
art-89: The Confederation is responsible for setting the main lines of inter-State transport policy, including road, rail, maritime and air infrastructure, in collaboration with the confederated States, and ensures the coordination required for the proper functioning …
art-90: The Confederation legislates on road traffic.
art-91: The Confederation and the confederated States ensure that adequate road infrastructure is available in all regions of the country.
art-91bis: Classified roads fall into two categories:
art-92: The Confederation may levy a performance-related or consumption-related charge on heavy vehicle traffic if such traffic causes costs to the general public that are not covered by other charges or fees.
art-93: Charge for the use of confederal roads
The Confederation levies a charge, in the form of a vignette, for the use of the confederal roads by motor vehicles and trailers that are not subject to the heavy vehicle charge.
art-94: Fund for confederal roads and transport infrastructure
The funding of the confederal roads and of contributions to measures to improve transport infrastructure in cities and conurbations that is related to road traffic is provided by a fund.
art-95: Railways and other modes of transport
Legislation on rail transport, cableways, maritime and inland navigation, and aviation is the responsibility of the Confederation.
art-95bis: The Confederation builds and operates a high-speed railway line, the Transbalkanska, linking Ļubļana, Zagreb, Beograd and Sofija, with a branch to Sarajevo.
art-96: Within the scope of their powers, the Confederation and the confederated States endeavour to ensure a sufficient, diverse, safe, economic and environmentally sustainable energy supply as well as the economic and efficient use of energy.
art-96bis: The Confederation maintains a public radio and television broadcaster, the Konfederalna Radio-Televizija (KRT). Its independence and autonomy in programming are guaranteed (Article 96).
art-97: The Confederation and the confederated States abide by the principle of economic freedom (Article 28). They jointly safeguard the interests of the Balkan economy.
art-97bis: The Confederal Central Bank (Konfederalna Centralna Banka) is directed by a governing board of five members, chosen for their competence in monetary and financial matters.
art-98: Housing, employment, social security and health
The Confederation encourages the construction of housing and home ownership.
art-98bis: The Confederation and the States encourage births and support families.
art-99: Civil law, criminal law, metrology and residence of foreign nationals
Legislation in the field of civil law and the law of civil procedure is the responsibility of the Confederation.
art-99bis: The Confederation balances its expenditure and revenue over time.
art-99ter: The Confederation levies only the taxes assigned to it by the Constitution. Other taxes belong to the States and, as their law provides, to the municipalities (Article 3).
art-99quater: The Confederation may levy a direct tax:
art-99quinquies: The Confederation lays down the principles for the harmonisation of the direct taxes of the Confederation, the States and the municipalities; it takes account of the efforts of the States towards harmonisation.
art-99sexies: The Confederation may levy a value added tax on the supply of goods and services, including supplies to oneself, and on imports, at a standard rate of no more than eighteen per cent and a reduced rate of no more than eight per cent.
art-99septies: In addition to customs duties and the taxes provided for in Article 97, the Confederation may levy:
art-100: The organs of the Confederation are:
art-101: The legislative, executive and judicial functions are separate.
art-101bis: Members of the Kongres, the Narodni Sabor and the Konfederalno Veće, and the Chancellor of the Confederation, bear no legal liability for the votes they cast and the statements they make before the chambers and their organs. This immunity may be neither lifted…
art-102: The Confederation recognises seven constituent peoples:
art-103: The Kongres is the principal legislative organ of the Confederation.
art-104: Delegates to the Kongres are elected by proportional list voting.
art-106: The Kongres elects from among its members a president and two vice-presidents. The three may not belong to the same constituent people.
art-106bis: The right of legislative initiative belongs:
art-107: The Narodni Sabor is the organ representing the constituent peoples of the Confederation.
art-108: Members of the Narodni Sabor are elected by direct universal suffrage by the citizens registered in the corresponding national register.
art-109: The Narodni Sabor exercises the following competences:
art-110: The Narodni Sabor elects a president from among its members. The presidency rotates each year among the national delegations, in the following order: Slovene, Croat, Serb, Bosniak, Montenegrin, Macedonian, Bulgarian.
art-110bis: When transmitting an adopted law to the Narodni Sabor, the President of the Kongres states whether it falls under the right of mandatory consent (Article 109 a).
art-110ter: The conciliation committee is composed of fourteen members: for each constituent people, one delegate appointed by the Kongres from among its members and one member appointed by the national delegation in the Narodni Sabor.
art-111: The Konfederalno Veće is the collegial executive organ of the Confederation.
art-112: Each national delegation of the Narodni Sabor proposes one candidate for the office of confederal councillor of its nation. The candidate is elected by simple majority within his national delegation.
art-112bis: If a seat on the Konfederalno Veće falls vacant, the national delegation concerned proposes a replacement within thirty days. He is elected under the procedure of Article 112 for the remainder of the term.
art-113: The presidency of the Confederation is held in turn by each member of the Konfederalno Veće for one year.
art-114: Each member of the Konfederalno Veće heads a confederal department. The departments are:
art-115: Members of the Konfederalno Veće may hold no other public office, elected mandate or private gainful activity during their term.
art-115bis: The Confederal Chancellery (Konfederalna Kancelarija) is the general staff of the Konfederalno Veće. It is directed by the Chancellor of the Confederation (kancelar Konfederacije), elected by the Confederal Assembly by absolute majority on the proposal of the …
art-116: The Ustavni Sud is the supreme judicial organ of the Confederation in constitutional matters.
art-117: For each seat to be filled, the national delegation of the people concerned proposes three candidates.
art-119: The judges of the Ustavni Sud exercise their office in full independence. They may receive instructions from no organ of the Confederation, no State and no national delegation.
art-119bis: The Confederal Court of Justice (Konfederalni Sud) is the supreme judicial authority of the Confederation, subject to the competences of the Ustavni Sud.
art-119ter: The Confederal Prosecutor's Office (Konfederalno Tužilaštvo) conducts prosecutions for offences within the competence of the Konfederalni Istražni Biro (Article 141). The Bureau reports to it on its investigations; the Prosecutor's Office decides whether to pr…
art-120: Each State guarantees its citizens the exercise of direct democracy.
art-121: Three hundred thousand citizens of the Confederation may, within eighteen months, propose the total or partial revision of the Confederal Constitution by way of popular initiative (Articles 148 and 149).
art-122: One hundred and fifty thousand citizens, or twelve States of which no more than half belong to the same constituent people (Article 1 bis), may request that any confederal law passed by the Kongres be submitted to the vote of the people.
art-123: The following are mandatorily submitted to the vote of the people and of the States:
art-123bis: A confederal law whose entry into force admits no delay may be declared urgent by the Kongres by an absolute majority of its members, with the approval of the Narodni Sabor by an absolute majority of its members and a simple majority in at least five of the se…
art-124: Where the Constitution requires a double majority, the result of the popular vote in each State determines the vote of that State.
art-124bis: Confederal popular votes are held on a Sunday, on the same day throughout the Confederation.
art-125: Each State freely establishes its institutions in accordance with the Confederal Constitution.
art-126: Each State freely adopts its flag, its coat of arms and its anthem.
art-127: Each State determines its official language within the regional South Slavic standard corresponding to its constituent people.
art-128: The national language of the Confederation is South Slavic (južnoslovenski jezik).
art-129: The official alphabet of the Confederation is the unified South Slavic Latin alphabet, composed of thirty-two letters:
art-130: No one may be compelled to use a regional standard or an alphabet other than the one of his choice.
art-130bis: The Confederal Language Institute (Konfederalni Institut za Jezik), an independent institution, has its seat in Ohrid.
art-130ter: The Confederation and the confederated States foster cohesion between the constituent peoples, the communities and the States (Article 2).
art-130quater: Political parties contribute to forming the opinion and the will of citizens.
art-130quinquies: Every pupil in upper secondary education, general or vocational, spends one semester of his schooling in a territorial State belonging to a constituent people other than that of the State in which he is schooled. A pupil schooled in a confederal territory or i…
art-130sexies: The curricula of compulsory education include a common core of history of the Confederation, of its peoples and of its communities, which the Confederation sets with the States.
art-130septies: The Confederation honours, in the confederal pantheon, persons whose life or work crossed the borders between the peoples and between the States.
art-130octies: The Day of the Confederation (Dan Konfederacije) is the anniversary of the acceptance of this Constitution by the people and the States (Article 151). It is a public holiday throughout the Confederation.
art-131: The Confederation ensures financial equalisation between its States in order to guarantee real equality of opportunity among citizens and the balanced development of the confederal territory.
art-132: Confederal law sets the equalisation formula according to the following principles:
art-133: The confederal department of Finance and the Treasury publishes each year a public report detailing, State by State, the financial flows between the Confederation and the States: confederal revenue collected, allocations paid, equalisation received or contribu…
art-134: Confederal investment in transport, communications, energy and research infrastructure, and in cultural facilities of confederal interest, is distributed according to the principle of geographic proportionality.
art-135: For each multi-year investment programme, confederal law sets distribution targets:
art-136: Any State that considers itself wronged by the distribution of a confederal investment programme may refer the matter to the Ustavni Sud.
art-136bis: The Confederal Court of Audit (Konfederalni Računski Sud) is the independent organ for the control of the finances of the Confederation.
art-137: Public security is first and foremost a matter for the States. Each State has its own police, in accordance with Article 125; the same applies to the confederal territories.
art-138: The Confederation has two security forces, distinct in nature, supervising authority and missions:
art-138bis: Inspector General of the security forces

The Inspector General of the confederal security forces (generalni inspektor sigurnosnih snaga) investigates complaints concerning the action of the Konfederalna Žandarmerija, the Konfederalni Istražni Biro and the Konfederalna Obavěštajna Agencija. Any person…
art-138ter: The Kongres and the Narodni Sabor form a joint security oversight committee (Komisija za Nadzor Sigurnosti) of fourteen members: for each constituent people, one delegate appointed by the Kongres from among its members and one member appointed by the national …
art-139: The Konfederalna Žandarmerija is competent for:
art-139bis: The Granična Straža checks every person crossing the external borders of the Confederation, on entry and on exit. The entries and exits of foreign nationals are recorded.
art-140: The Konfederalna Žandarmerija is a corps with military status as regards its organisation, hierarchy and discipline. Its officers are called žandarmi; the officers of the Granična Straža are called stražari. It carries out its police missions under the functio…
art-140bis: A specialised intervention unit is established within the Konfederalna Žandarmerija, responsible for counter-terrorism, hostage rescue and very high-risk interventions falling within confederal competence.
art-141: The Konfederalni Istražni Biro is an investigative agency without community-policing competence. It performs no territorial patrolling function.
art-142: The Konfederalni Istražni Biro has its own officers empowered to make arrests and to conduct apprehension operations within its enumerated competence.
art-143: The Konfederalni Istražni Biro is directed by a board of three members: a director-general and two deputy directors. The three may not belong to the same constituent people.
art-144: Any investigation of the Konfederalni Istražni Biro targeting a confederal or State elected official, a member of a State government or a judge, or bearing directly on the competences of a State, requires the prior authorisation of a special chamber of the Ust…
art-145: The Konfederalni Istražni Biro is prohibited from:
art-145bis: The Konfederalna Obavěštajna Agencija (Confederal Intelligence Agency) collects and analyses the information necessary for the security of the Confederation. It has its seat in Sarajevo and comprises an external branch and an internal branch.
art-145ter: Direction and oversight of the Agency
The Agency is placed under the collegial authority of the Konfederalno Veće; no councillor directs it alone.
art-146: In the event of a serious and imminent threat to the existence of the Confederation, its constitutional order or the safety of the population, or in the event of a major disaster, the Konfederalno Veće may declare a state of emergency over all or part of the t…
art-147: The Constitution may be revised totally or partially at any time.
art-148: A total revision may be proposed by the people (Article 121), by the Kongres or by the Narodni Sabor.
art-149: A partial revision may be requested by the people (Article 121) or decided by the Kongres.
art-150: The following provisions may be revised only with the approval of the Narodni Sabor by a two-thirds majority in plenary assembly and a majority within each of the seven national delegations:
art-151: This Constitution enters into force on the first day of the sixth month following its acceptance by the people and the States.
art-152: The first elections to the Kongres and the Narodni Sabor are held on the same day, no later than six months after this Constitution enters into force.
art-153: The Confederal Assembly meets within thirty days of the first elections. It elects the members of the Konfederalno Veće and the Chancellor of the Confederation. The term of the first Konfederalno Veće ends with the first legislative term.
art-154: The national registers open on the day this Constitution enters into force.
art-155: The law in force on the territory of the Confederation when this Constitution enters into force remains applicable in so far as it is not contrary to it, until it is replaced by the competent confederal or State law.
art-156: The States continue to levy the general consumption taxes they levy when this Constitution enters into force until the confederal value added tax is introduced, no later than three years after that date (Article 99 sexies).
